look: Grand new stone blocks four or five floors high, with shops and cafés below, beside older palaces and museums. Berlin had grown fast to about 1.8 million people.
Men in dark suits with bowler hats, top hats or straw boaters, many with big moustaches. Women in long skirts, puffed sleeves and wide hats. Soldiers in spiked helmets.
Electric trams, horse buses and cabs. The first underground and elevated railway line opened in 1902.
Bright electric arc lamps on the big streets and squares, gas lamps on the rest.
Kaiser Wilhelm II ruled the German Empire, and Berlin had been its capital since 1871.

stops.name: Unter den Linden at Café Bauer
stops.title: Unter den Linden, Café Bauer
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: A famous Viennese-style café on the corner of Friedrichstraße, with newspapers from all over the world.
spots.how: Its name is written across the front.

spots.d: Round columns for posters, invented by the Berlin printer Ernst Litfaß in 1854.
spots.how: Germans still call them Litfaß columns.

spots.d: A bus pulled by horses, with seats on the roof.
spots.how: Electric trams were taking over at this time.

spots.d: Crowds of people in hats on the city's grandest street.
spots.how: Unter den Linden ran from the royal palace to the Brandenburg Gate.

stops.name: The New Guardhouse
stops.title: Berlin, Neue Wache
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: Built from 1816 to 1818 by the architect Karl Friedrich Schinkel for the king's guard.
spots.how: It still stands on Unter den Linden.

spots.d: The changing of the guard here drew crowds every day.
spots.how: You can see the line of soldiers in front of the guardhouse.

spots.d: Statues of generals from the wars against Napoleon stood in front.
spots.how: They were made by the sculptor Christian Daniel Rauch.

spots.d: A cart with the shop's name painted on the side.
spots.how: Shops delivered goods by horse and cart.

stops.name: Potsdamer Platz
stops.title: Berlin, Potsdamer Platz
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: Potsdamer Platz was one of the busiest crossings in Europe, full of trams, buses and cabs.
spots.how: Look at the traffic jam across the square.

spots.d: Her puffed sleeves and long skirt and his hat are the fashion of about 1900.
spots.how: Fashion pictures of the time show the same shapes.

spots.d: Capes and long coats kept out the wind.

stops.name: The Neptune Fountain and the Palace
stops.title: Berlin, Neptunbrunnen
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: Unveiled in 1891: the sea god with four women for Germany's great rivers, the Rhine, Elbe, Oder and Vistula.
spots.how: The fountain still stands in Berlin, in a different spot.

spots.d: Home of the Prussian kings and German emperors. It was damaged in the Second World War and blown up in 1950.
spots.how: Its front has been rebuilt and is now the Humboldt Forum.

spots.d: A horse-drawn coach passes the palace.
spots.how: There were no cars on this square yet.
